name: exe.dev

modes.label: Work pool (current; reserved pool billed hourly 24/7, shared by all VMs)
modes.commit_note: Work: $150/month paid in advance covers 4 vCPU / 8 GB of capacity across all pools AND standalone VMs; capacity beyond is metered hourly at $0.105 per 2 vCPU ($0.0525/vCPU-h) only while it exists (month = 150 + (vcpu-4) * 0.0525 * 730). Any even vCPU count 4..512 allowed (subset listed). Pools are billed empty or full. Pools up to 32 vCPU take effect immediately; 34-512 vCPU need support approval (pending pools are not billed). Unlimited pools. Shrinking is immediate; hourly metering after resize is documented.
modes.note: Utilisation-independent; stopped/idle VMs free pool capacity. VMs per pool = min(1000, 25 x vCPU), now documented (4 vCPU=100, 32=800); no team-wide VM limit. CLI --max-vms default 100 but adjustable. Pools above 32 vCPU need support approval. Included disk 100 GB per 2 vCPU and bandwidth 50 GB per vCPU, per pool (docs/billing/work.md; no 800 GB cap stated).

modes.label: Personal pool (current; 2/4/8/16 vCPU at $15/$35/$75/$155)
modes.commit_note: Flat monthly, paid upfront, prorated on change. Selector 2/4/8/16 vCPU = $15/$35/$75/$155 (embedded pricing-scale JSON 'personal:monthly:20260914' on exe.dev/pricing, verified 2026-09-28). Max 16 vCPU/32 GB, 1 pool.
modes.note: Personal pool placed in user's region only.

modes.label: Standalone / sandbox VMs (current; per VM, own reserved capacity)
modes.note: $0.105 per 2 vCPU per hour, RAM bundled (default 2 vCPU/8 GB; max 16/32 Personal, 32/64 Work). ram_per_vcpu max 4 inferred from default size. Billed by the hour for as long as the VM exists: a STOPPED standalone VM keeps its reserved capacity and is still billed in full; only deleting it stops billing (stop-and-keep workflows are understated by the engine). Personal: any account can create them, billed on top of the subscription. Work: enabled by a team admin setting; standalone vCPU counts toward the 4 included vCPU and each VM carries its own disk/bandwidth allowance. Legacy Individual/Team plans cannot create standalone VMs.

modes.label: Usage / Cloud Pool (sales-only, per second, peak-hourly CPU + active memory)
modes.commit_note: Not self-serve: contact support@exe.dev. Minimum commitment/plan fee unknown.
modes.note: CPU billed per core on PEAK usage within each hour (so 'active' understates bursty loads); memory billed on active memory; idle VMs: no CPU, memory at disk rate ($0.08/GiB-month). Basis verified 2026-09-28: "CPU and active memory bill by peak hourly usage; idle VMs drop to disk-only." (https://exe.dev/sandbox). What makes a VM "idle" is not defined; modelled as auto_stop_idle. Sales flag kept: exe.dev/sandbox says 'Contact us about usage pricing'; as of 2026-09-29 docs/billing/cloud-pool.md is gone and the billing docs list only Personal/Work/Enterprise (+legacy), so this Cloud Pool may be retired or folded into Enterprise.

modes.label: Legacy Individual pool tiers ($20-$160; pre-Sep-2026, still in billing docs)
modes.commit_note: Superseded on public pricing page by Personal/Work (live 2026-09-28); availability to new customers doubtful, grandfathering unverified. Team variant $25/$50/$100/$200 per user gives each user their own pool (burst into teammates' idle capacity) - not representable as a single tier. Enterprise 'from' price; max_vms 'thousands' (null).
modes.note: Includes $20/mo Shelley LLM credit (not usable for compute).

plans.name: Personal
plans.note: $15/mo = 2 vCPU/4 GB pool and also the minimum monthly spend (fee_is_credit models 'min spend'). 1 pool, 50 VMs. Included disk scales with capacity: 2 vCPU 100 GB / 4 vCPU 200 GB / 8 vCPU 400 GB / 16 vCPU 800 GB (docs/billing/personal.md); bandwidth 200 GB at every size. Standalone VMs billed hourly on top of the subscription (max 16 vCPU/32 GB). No monthly Shelley credit.

plans.name: Work
plans.note: $150/month paid in advance, covering 4 vCPU / 8 GB of capacity (pools + standalone VMs combined); extra capacity $0.105 per 2 vCPU-h, billed hourly only while it exists. Not per seat; unlimited users, SSO. Pools up to 512 vCPU/1024 GB (above 32 vCPU needs support approval); unlimited pools in any region; up to 25 VMs per vCPU, max 1000 per pool; concurrency null because pools are not capped. Disk 100 GB per 2 vCPU and bandwidth 50 GB per vCPU per pool (allowances do not move between pools); docs state no 800 GB cap.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Custom pricing: dedicated hardware, BYOC/AWS-GCP VPC, nested virtualization, Slack support, SLA. Legacy page: from $35.84/h for 512 vCPU/2048 GB.

plans.name: Legacy Individual (Small..XLarge)
plans.note: No longer sold (existing subscribers only; one-year migration window from 2026-09-28). Included disk scales 100/200/400/800 GB by size. No standalone VMs.

plans.name: Legacy Team (per user)
plans.note: No longer sold (existing teams only; new teams choose Work). $25/$50/$100/$200 per user for Small/Medium/Large/XLarge per-user pools; every member counts the same, prorated mid-cycle; 50 VMs, 100 GB disk, 250 GB transfer per user; burst into teammates' idle capacity; SSO; no standalone VMs. per_seat shown for Small.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.
caveats: Three conflicting price surfaces. Live /pricing and /docs/pricing (2026-09-28) show the NEW model: Personal $15 (2 vCPU/4 GB), Work $0.21/h per 4 vCPU/8 GB (min $150), standalone VMs $0.105/2 vCPU-h. docs/billing/overview.md and the /sandbox page still show LEGACY $20/$40/$80/$160 pools (documented as current as late as 2026-09-09). The /sandbox usage rates ($0.05/core-h, $0.016/GiB-h) are sales-only 'Cloud Pool'.

Work pool prices confirmed linear from the embedded pricing JSON (4/8/16/32/64/128/256/512 vCPU = $0.21/$0.42/$0.84/$1.68/$3.36/$6.72/$13.44/$26.88 per h); intermediate even sizes (CLI allows any even 4..512) interpolated at the same $0.0525/vCPU-h.
Personal pool sizes 2/4/8/16 vCPU = $15/$35/$75/$155 per month (embedded pricing JSON on exe.dev/pricing, verified 2026-09-28). Note 4 vCPU/8 GB is $35, not 2x$15.
Pools bill regardless of utilisation; engine should size by peak concurrent vCPU/RAM. Resizing pools off-hours can reduce cost (not modelled; hourly proration assumed but undocumented).
Standalone VM billing granularity, minimum, and whether stopped standalone VMs bill are undocumented; RAM is bundled (default 4 GiB/vCPU, max 2 GiB/vCPU at top size).
Usage pricing bills CPU on PEAK usage within each hour, so 'active' basis understates cost for bursty loads; memory billed on 'active' memory (definition unclear). Minimum commitment unknown.

included_disk_gib (100) is POOLED per account/user (Work: 100 GB per 2 vCPU of pool), not per sandbox. Disk measured as time-averaged ext4 filesystem usage, not provisioned size. Default VM disk 25 GB, grow-only.
No snapshots: retained state = stopped VM disk (or cp clone), billed as disk at $0.08/GB-month beyond allowance.

Egress allowance: 200 GB (Personal, any size; legacy Individual), 250 GB per user (legacy Team), Work 50 GB per vCPU of pool (200 GB at 4 vCPU, capped at 800 GB) - the '200 GB' bullet is the 4-vCPU value, not a conflict. Overage $0.05/GiB billed at cycle end; inbound never billed.
Standalone VMs and pools require support/team approval.
No free compute tier; 30-day trial via invite; invite rewards (credits/memory/disk) amounts unpublished. Legacy plans include $20/mo Shelley LLM credit (not compute).
No dedicated IPv4 (shared per-owner IPv4 pool; HTTPS proxy + SSH only). Account bound to one region (Personal); Work pools in any region; no regional price differences found.
AWS/Azure Marketplace billing exists (legacy sizes); marketplace prices not retrieved.
No benchmark data for exe-dev in research/benchmarks.json.

Usage-based (sales-only) mode: CPU and active memory bill on the PEAK of each hour, so set the peak CPU/RAM inputs, not the averages. "Active memory" is not defined (page cache inclusion unknown); the idle trigger that drops a VM to disk-only billing is not documented.
Usage-priced Cloud Pool ($0.05/core-h peak, $0.016/GiB-h active memory, exe.dev/sandbox) is not self-serve: the billing docs say to email support@exe.dev, so the mode keeps the sales flag.

Pricing changed 2026-09-28 (blog 'Pools: Our Newest Primitive'): Personal/Work replaced Individual/Team; existing customers have one year to migrate. Personal/Work/Enterprise include no monthly Shelley credit.
A pool pending support approval is not billed; pool billing stops when the pool is deleted; pools reserve CPU+memory only, not disk.
Switching Personal -> Work cancels Personal immediately with no automatic credit for the rest of the cycle (refund on request).

Approval (docs 2026-09-29): Personal standalone VMs need no approval; Work standalone VMs need a team-admin setting (off by default); pools up to 32 vCPU are immediate, 34-512 vCPU need exe.dev support approval. Supersedes the older 'Standalone VMs and pools require support/team approval' caveat.

fleet.tiers: Personal pool up to 50 VMs (shared 2–16 vCPU pool); Work table 1,000 VMs/pool with larger resource pools. Standalone sandboxes separately 50 Personal / 100 Work; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Entry 50 is a VM-count allowance, not 50 full-size dedicated machines: a selected CPU/RAM pool is shared. New paid Personal pool starts 2 vCPU/4 GB. Work top-card count 100 and comparison pool count 1,000 describe inconsistent/different modes; use mode-specific confirmation before 300/1,000. No assumed instant custom allocation.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: A stopped standalone VM is not billed for its vCPU and memory. It keeps its disk, and it still counts toward your VM limits.
snapshot_auto.note: State = persistent disk only; no snapshot/checkpoint/suspend mechanism anywhere in llms-full.txt (0 hits for 'snapshot'/'checkpoint'). VMs are not auto-stopped on idle. Docs say disks are 'persisted and backed up' (backups, not this feature).

snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/restore command in the full CLI reference. Closest thing: `cp` = copy-on-write clone of a VM ('clone disk and config', /sandbox page) into a NEW VM, disk only, no memory. A stopped cp copy can serve as a manual disk checkpoint / template for further cp, but there is no restore-in-place or named snapshot.

harness_api.quote: Send a prompt to Shelley on a VM ... shelley prompt [--model=<model>] [--reasoning=<level>] <vm> <prompt>
harness_api.note: Shelley only (exe.dev's own web coding agent). Also `new --prompt` ('initial prompt to send to Shelley after VM creation'). Driveable over SSH and the HTTPS /exec API (which runs the same command set). No documented API to stream Shelley events, list/resume conversations, or drive Claude Code/Codex/Pi (preinstalled, but only via shell exec). exe.dev also serves an MCP server at https://exe.dev/mcp (tool list not documented).

egress_allowlist.quote: On the networking side, we don't give your VM its own public IP. Instead, we terminate HTTPS/TLS requests, and proxy them securely to your VM's web servers.
egress_allowlist.note: No firewall/allowlist/egress-rule/no-internet option appears on `new`, `share`, `team`, or `pool` in the full CLI/docs reference (only two unrelated hits for 'allowlist', about API-key scoping and a third-party Slack bot's own allowlist). VMs get unrestricted outbound internet by default; secrets are protected via the integrations proxy rather than by blocking egress.

egress_http_rules.note: Not documented. The http-proxy integration only fixes a target host, injects headers and can strip a path prefix (`--strip-prefix`); it does not filter methods/paths, and direct internet egress is unrestricted anyway.

ingress_rules.quote: By default, only users with access to the VM can access the HTTP proxy. Users accessing https://vmname.exe.xyz/ for the first time will be redirected to log into `exe.dev`.
ingress_rules.note: Private-by-default auth-gated HTTPS proxy; `share set-public/set-private`; per-person Web or Root shares, team sharing controls; ports 3000-9999 forwarded only to authorized users; 'You may only mark a single port public'. No public IP; only HTTPS proxy + brokered SSH reach the VM. VM-scoped bearer tokens for programmatic access. No IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VM (Cloud Hypervisor) with root and systemd; user cannot pick the kernel but the stock kernel presumably includes netfilter (Docker runs inside, which needs iptables/nftables).

secret_proxy.quote: Whatever the type, the secret is stored server-side and injected at the network edge when your VM calls the integration hostname. The VM — and any agent running on it — can *use* the integration but can never read the secret.
secret_proxy.note: Integrations: HTTP proxy (any target host; --header/--bearer/basic auth injected at <name>.int.exe.xyz), S3 SigV4 signing, GitHub App (git over HTTPS), LLM providers, Slack/Discord bots, VM-to-VM, token-mint, OCI registry pull tokens, 100+ catalog services, AWS/GCP workload identity federation. Attach per VM, per tag or auto:all. The VM calls a special hostname (explicit proxy endpoint, not transparent interception). HTTP(S) only; no DB/SSH protocol injection documented (git via GitHub integration over HTTPS).

volume_attach.note: No attach/detach-volume command exists in the full CLI reference (`new`, `resize`, `cp`, `pool`, `team`, `billing`, `share`, `integrations` — no `volume` subcommand). Disk is fixed to the VM it was created/resized on.

volume_shared.quote: exe.dev [...] gives you virtual machines [...] create a virtual private network to connect their VMs. Tailscale
volume_shared.note: No shared-filesystem/shared-volume feature is documented anywhere; cross-VM data sharing is only via Tailscale private networking, SSH/scp/rsync, the VM-to-VM integration, or the S3 integration — none of which is a shared mounted volume.

desktop.quote: It should be some kind of stock linux ... Just a computer.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — exe.dev is an SSH/terminal-accessed Linux VM product (root, systemd, Docker); no VNC/RDP/streamed graphical desktop is documented anywhere in the docs or CLI reference.

anti_bot.quote: create a VM a computer, in about a second
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — exe.dev sells general-purpose Linux VMs for coding agents, not a browser-automation/scraping product; no stealth or anti-fingerprinting feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: create a VM a computer, in about a second
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving feature is documented anywhere in the docs/CLI/API reference; exe.dev is a generic dev VM, not a scraping/automation service.

egress_ip_type.quote: No dedicated IPv4 (shared per-owner IPv4 pool; HTTPS proxy + SSH only).
egress_ip_type.note: network.ipv4_available is false and no static/residential/mobile IP feature is documented; VMs egress through the provider's shared cloud-hosted datacenter IP space with no dedicated/static assignment.

pause_resume.quote: A stopped standalone VM is not billed for its vCPU and memory. It keeps its disk, and it still counts toward your VM limits.
pause_resume.note: Stopping a VM halts vCPU/memory billing (disk still billed) and it can be started again later; this is the product's pause/resume mechanism, with billing reduced while stopped.

wake_on_request.quote: The VM must be running or stopped.
wake_on_request.note: No documentation of a stopped/sleeping VM automatically waking on an incoming SSH/HTTPS request; starting a stopped VM requires an explicit start action (CLI/API), not a passive wake-on-request trigger.

own_agent_api.quote: Send a prompt to Shelley on a VM ... shelley prompt [--model=<model>] [--reasoning=<level>] <vm> <prompt>
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Shelley is exe.dev's own CODING agent/harness (already modeled as harness_api/agent_harnesses), not a browser/computer-use/research task agent; exe.dev has no desktop or browser-control product for such an agent to drive.

mcp_server.quote: exe.dev serves a Model Context Protocol server at https://exe.dev/mcp. Point your favorite MCP client at it
mcp_server.note: First-party MCP server for controlling exe.dev VMs from Claude Code and other MCP clients.

lang_node.quote: make python3-pip python-is-python3 ... docker.io docker-buildx docker-compose-v2 ...
lang_node.note: The default exeuntu image's package list installs Go, Python3/pip, and many tools but no Node.js/npm; docs note installing the Codex npm package 'works too if you prefer the Node-packaged build and already have a modern Node on the VM,' implying Node is not preinstalled out of the box (though it can be apt-installed manually).

static_egress_ip.quote: No dedicated IPv4 (shared per-owner IPv4 pool; HTTPS proxy + SSH only).
static_egress_ip.note: No static/dedicated outbound IP feature is documented; VMs share a per-owner IPv4 pool with no fixed per-VM address, consistent with network.ipv4_available=false in the card.

max_session_h.quote: A standalone VM ... does not share capacity with your other VMs. It is billed by the hour while it runs.
max_session_h.note: VMs (pool or standalone) run until explicitly stopped or deleted by the user/API; no maximum session/lifetime duration is documented anywhere in the extensive CLI/API/billing docs.

snapshot.note: No contradiction: exe.dev has no snapshot/checkpoint/restore mechanism. `cp` is a disk+config copy-on-write clone into a NEW VM (not a snapshot of the source that can be restored in place), and `--memory` there just sets the new VM's RAM allocation, not a captured memory image. 'snapshot' and 'checkpoint' do not appear anywhere in llms-full.txt. Card's existing feature_evidence.snapshot_auto/snapshot_on_demand (false/false) already document this; 'none' plus fork=true (disk clone) is consistent, not contradictory.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: The only fork/clone primitive (`cp`) copies disk and config into a new VM; `--memory` sets the new VM's RAM size, it does not carry over live RAM contents. No memory-state snapshot/restore appears anywhere in llms-full.txt.

nested_virt.quote: Nested virtualization (KVM) | Not included | Not included | Included
nested_virt.note: The live pricing comparison table lists 'Nested virtualization (KVM)' as a named feature: Not included on Personal and Work, but Included on Enterprise. This matches the card's own Enterprise plan note ('dedicated hardware, BYOC/AWS-GCP VPC, nested virtualization, Slack support, SLA'). So nested_virt is offered (Enterprise/custom tier), not a flat no — correct to true.

computer_use.quote: On the networking side, we don't give your VM its own public IP. Instead, we terminate HTTPS/TLS requests, and proxy them securely to your VM's web servers. For SSH, we handle `ssh vmname.exe.xyz`.
computer_use.note: No mention of VNC, remote desktop, screen-share, browser-automation/computer-use API, or GUI streaming anywhere in llms-full.txt or the pricing/sandbox pages. Access is SSH + HTTPS proxy to a headless Linux VM; product is a coding-agent dev-env VM, not a computer-use/GUI-agent product.

auto_stop_idle.quote: A stopped standalone VM is not billed for its vCPU and memory. It keeps its disk, and it still counts toward your VM limits.
auto_stop_idle.note: No occurrence of 'idle' anywhere in llms-full.txt for the self-serve Personal/Work/standalone-VM products; stopping is always a manual/CLI action, never an automatic idle-timeout. (The sales-only, non-self-serve 'Cloud Pool' usage mode is separately modeled with auto_stop_idle:true inside its own mode entry, which is correct and distinct from this top-level flag.)

volumes.note: The word 'volume' does not occur anywhere in llms-full.txt or the CLI reference. Storage is only each VM's own grow-only local disk (`new --disk`, `resize`); no separate attachable/mountable volume object exists.

public_ipv4.quote: On the networking side, we don't give your VM its own public IP. Instead, we terminate HTTPS/TLS requests, and proxy them securely to your VM's web servers. For SSH, we handle `ssh vmname.exe.xyz`.
public_ipv4.note: Explicit statement that VMs never get their own public IP; reachability is only via the shared HTTPS proxy and brokered SSH hostname.

gpu.quote: Personal $15/month ... Work $0.21/hour ... Enterprise Custom resource limits Dedicated hardware and resources ...
gpu.note: No 'GPU'/'nvidia'/'cuda' term appears anywhere in llms-full.txt, the pricing comparison table, or the sandbox usage page; all plan resources are described purely in vCPU/RAM/disk/bandwidth. Product is CPU-only cloud-hypervisor KVM VMs for coding agents.

windows.quote: With most providers, your VM starts with a "base image" and is given a block device. Exe.dev instead starts with a container image (by default, "exeuntu"), and hooks it up with a block device with the image on it.
windows.note: No 'Windows' term appears anywhere in the docs; VMs boot a Linux container-derived image ('exeuntu') under Cloud Hypervisor. Windows guests are plainly outside what this Linux dev-env sandbox product offers.

macos.quote: Exe.dev instead starts with a container image (by default, "exeuntu"), and hooks it up with a block device with the image on it.
macos.note: No 'macOS'/'Mac OS'/'Darwin' guest term appears anywhere in the docs; this is a Linux-VM-only sandbox provider (KVM/Cloud Hypervisor), and macOS guests are outside the product by construction (no bare-metal Mac hardware offering).

arm64.quote: case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64) A=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl ;; aarch64|arm64) A=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl ;;
arm64.note: The only aarch64/arm64 references in the docs are about which CLI-tool binary to download on the OPERATOR'S own machine (client side), not about the guest VM architecture; there is no mention anywhere of an arm64 guest VM option, and Cloud Hypervisor VM sizing/pricing is undifferentiated by CPU architecture, implying x86_64-only guests.

self_host.quote: These providers host the virtual machines and compute that our customers
self_host.note: exe.dev is a hosted SaaS platform run by exe.dev on its own/partner infrastructure; there is no offering to run the exe.dev control plane on a customer's own infrastructure. The Enterprise 'Bring your own cloud' (BYOC, AWS/GCP VPC) option still means exe.dev's control plane placing VMs inside the customer's cloud account, not the customer self-hosting the exe.dev product itself.

open_source.quote: The [Dockerfile for exeuntu](https://github.com/boldsoftware/exeuntu/blob/main/Dockerfile) is open source, so you can use that as a base if you'd like.
open_source.note: Only the default VM base-image Dockerfile ('exeuntu') is published as open source; the exe.dev platform itself (control plane, CLI backend, billing, proxy) is closed-source SaaS with no public repository referenced anywhere in the docs.

fork_running.note: derived: the `cp` command (the only fork/clone primitive) copies a VM's disk and config into a new VM; nothing in the CLI reference, options, or examples requires the source VM to be stopped first, and the docs never mention a 'must be stopped' precondition anywhere for cp (searched). Memory state is not carried over (already modeled as memory_snapshot_fork=false), but the clone itself is not documented as requiring the source to be paused/stopped.

soc2.quote: E-mail security@exe.dev to disclose security vulnerabilities. exe.dev does not have a bounty program. Security Bulletins
soc2.note: exe.dev's own /security page is only a vulnerability-disclosure/bulletin feed; no mention of SOC 2 (or any compliance attestation) appears there, on the pricing/Enterprise page, or anywhere in llms-full.txt (0 hits for 'SOC' or 'compliance' as a certification). No trust-center/compliance page exists (site returns 404 for /trust, /compliance, /soc2).

hipaa.quote: E-mail security@exe.dev to disclose security vulnerabilities. exe.dev does not have a bounty program. Security Bulletins
hipaa.note: No mention of HIPAA, BAA, or 'business associate' anywhere in llms-full.txt, the security page, or the Enterprise plan docs (which list dedicated hardware/BYOC/SSO/SLA but no compliance certifications). No compliance/trust page exists on the site.
